name: Maurya
uniques: [1] Happiness from each type of luxury resource
startIntroPart1: I am Ashoka, who ruled Magadha and conquered Kalinga - and then, sickened by the bloodshed, laid down the sword forever.
startIntroPart2: I built my empire on Dhamma instead: edicts of compassion carved into stone and pillars, so that all who came after would remember that conquest by righteousness outlasts conquest by war.
introduction: I am Ashoka the Great, Emperor of Maurya. Let us speak as civilized rulers should.
declaringWar: I had hoped my edicts would be heard, but it seems force is the only language you understand.
defeated: The wheel of Dhamma turns even in defeat. My edicts will outlast both of our empires.
neutralHello: Peace and prosperity to you, traveler.
tradeRequest: Trade enriches both our peoples. Shall we make an agreement?

name: Gupta
startIntroPart1: I am Chandragupta the Second, Vikramaditya, Sun of Valor. Under my reign, Aryabhata charts the heavens and our scholars give the world the very concept of zero.
startIntroPart2: Poetry, mathematics, astronomy, and art flourish in my courts. History will call this age golden - let us see how brightly your civilization shines beside it.
introduction: Greetings. I am Chandragupta II of the Gupta Empire. Wisdom and strength both have their place at this table.
declaringWar: Even the wisest ruler must sometimes draw the sword. You leave me little choice.
defeated: Empires fall, but knowledge endures. What we have learned cannot be unconquered.
neutralHello: Welcome. What brings you to my court?
tradeRequest: Commerce between learned nations benefits us both.

name: Chola
startIntroPart1: I am Rajaraja Chola, Lord of the rising tides. My fleets have carried our banner to Lanka, the Maldives, and across the eastern seas to Srivijaya itself.
startIntroPart2: I have raised the great temple of Thanjavur to touch the sky, its tower built of solid granite. Let the world see what a kingdom of the sea can build on land.
introduction: I am Rajaraja Chola I. My ships rule the waters - I trust we can also find calmer seas between us.
declaringWar: The tide turns against you. My fleets and my armies will see this through.
defeated: The seas I commanded for so long now carry news of my fall. Remember the name Chola all the same.
neutralHello: The winds favor us today. Speak your purpose.
hateHello: You test my patience as the storms test my ships.
tradeRequest: A trade route between our lands would profit us both handsomely.

name: Mughals
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Culture] wonders [in all cities]
[1] Happiness from each type of luxury resource
startIntroPart1: I am Akbar, Padishah of the Mughals. I rule a realm of a hundred peoples and a hundred faiths, and I have learned that an empire endures by tolerance, not by the sword alone.
startIntroPart2: My architects raise forts of red sandstone and gardens of paradise; my court welcomes scholars of every creed. Let us see whether your civilization can match such grandeur.
introduction: I am Akbar. My empire spans many peoples bound together - I extend the same hand of peace to you.
declaringWar: I have offered every ruler tolerance and reason. You have chosen war instead - so be it.
defeated: An empire built on a hundred peoples does not vanish so easily. We will remember this.
neutralHello: Peace be upon you. What business brings you before the Peacock Throne?
hateHello: Choose your next words with care.
tradeRequest: Goods flow freely through my empire - let us open a route between our lands.

name: Vijayanagara
uniques: [+15]% Production when constructing [Culture] wonders [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Krishnadevaraya, ruler of Vijayanagara, the City of Victory. My markets overflow with diamonds, and my temples rise higher than any before them.
startIntroPart2: Poets and architects both call my court home. Let us see whether your realm can match such splendor.
introduction: I am Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara. Wealth and culture both flow from strength - let us speak as equals.
declaringWar: You coveted what my city built. Now you shall face the army that defends it.
defeated: The City of Victory has fallen at last. Its name will not be forgotten.
neutralHello: Welcome to my court. State your business.

name: Marathas
uniques: [+15]% Strength <for [All] units> <when fighting in [Friendly Land] tiles>
[+20]% Production when constructing [Mounted] units [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Shivaji, founder of Swarajya - self-rule. From the forts of the Sahyadri hills, I have humbled empires far larger than my own.
startIntroPart2: My horsemen strike like lightning and vanish into the hills before the enemy can answer. Test me at your own risk.
introduction: I am Shivaji. I did not inherit an empire - I carved one from the mountains. I extend you the same respect I'd want in return.
declaringWar: You mistake patience for weakness. My hill forts have humbled greater armies than yours.
defeated: A fort may fall, but the spirit of Swarajya does not die with it.

name: Delhi Sultanate
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Melee] units [in all cities]
[-15]% Gold cost of acquiring tiles [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Alauddin Khalji, Sultan of Delhi. I have fixed the prices of grain and cloth alike, and I have turned back the Mongol hordes at my gates.
startIntroPart2: An empire is built on discipline as much as conquest. You would do well to remember that.
introduction: I am Alauddin Khalji. My armies are vast and my treasury is full - choose your dealings with me carefully.
declaringWar: I turned back the Mongols themselves. You will fare no better.
defeated: Even the strictest discipline could not hold back fate forever.
neutralHello: State your business and be brief.

name: Pallava
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Culture] wonders [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Narasimhavarman, called Mamalla - the Great Wrestler. My sculptors carve entire temples from single boulders at Mahabalipuram, facing the eastern sea.
startIntroPart2: I have humbled the Chalukyas and sent my fleet across the waters to restore an ally's throne in Lanka. Let our two realms find more peaceful business.
introduction: I am Narasimhavarman of the Pallavas. My shore temples have stood against the sea itself - I trust we can build something lasting between us as well.
declaringWar: I have wrestled kings to the ground before. You will be no exception.
defeated: The waves will keep wearing at my shore temples, just as you have worn down my armies.
neutralHello: Peace to you. What brings you to Kanchipuram?

name: Chalukya
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Melee] units [in all cities]
[+15]% Strength <for [All] units> <when fighting in [Friendly Land] tiles>
startIntroPart1: I am Pulakeshin, second of my name. I halted the great Harsha himself at the Narmada and forced him to abandon his ambitions southward.
startIntroPart2: My capital at Badami is carved into red sandstone cliffs, fortress and temple alike. Cross me and you will learn why Harsha turned back.
introduction: I am Pulakeshin II of the Chalukyas. I have stopped greater armies than most - speak plainly with me.
declaringWar: Even Harsha learned the cost of marching against me. You will learn it too.
defeated: No fortress holds forever. Remember that I once held the line where even Harsha could not pass.
neutralHello: What business brings you before Badami's gates?

name: Rashtrakuta
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Culture] wonders [in all cities]
[+20]% Production towards any buildings that already exist in the Capital
startIntroPart1: I am Krishna of the Rashtrakutas. At Ellora I have ordered an entire temple carved downward from a single mountain of solid rock - the Kailasa, a mountain reshaped into a god's home.
startIntroPart2: What other ruler commands the very earth to become a monument? Show me what you have built.
introduction: I am Krishna I. My masons shape mountains into temples - I wonder what your civilization has shaped.
declaringWar: I carved a temple from solid stone. Carving through your defenses will be easier still.
defeated: Kailasa will stand long after this defeat is forgotten. Some things outlast even empires.
hateHello: Speak, and be done with it.

name: Kushan
startIntroPart1: I am Kanishka, ruler of a realm that bridges worlds - Greek, Persian, Indian, and Chinese caravans all cross my lands on the Silk Road.
startIntroPart2: Buddhist monks, Greek sculptors, and Central Asian horsemen all call my empire home. Trade with me, and prosper as my merchants do.
introduction: I am Kanishka of the Kushans. My empire connects every road worth traveling - let us open one between us.
declaringWar: My horse archers control every pass from here to the Silk Road's end. You will not enjoy crossing them as enemies.
defeated: The roads I built will carry on without me. Someone else will profit from what I made.
neutralHello: Welcome, traveler. The roads are safer when we are not enemies.

name: Satavahana
uniques: [1] Happiness from each type of luxury resource
startIntroPart1: I am Gautamiputra Satakarni, Lord of the Three Oceans. My ports on both coasts trade spices and cotton with Rome itself.
startIntroPart2: I have restored the honor of my line and humbled the foreign Shaka invaders. Let our caravans cross paths in peace.
introduction: I am Gautamiputra Satakarni of the Satavahanas. The Deccan's trade routes all answer to me - shall we put them to use?
declaringWar: I drove the Shakas from my lands. You will find me no gentler.
defeated: The trade routes I built will outlive this defeat, as they outlived every invader before you.
neutralHello: Welcome to the Deccan. What brings you here?

name: Pala
startIntroPart1: I am Dharmapala, ruler of Bengal. I have founded the great monastery of Vikramashila, where scholars come from as far as Tibet to study.
startIntroPart2: While others war over thrones, I build libraries that will outlast any throne. Let knowledge, not conquest, define our meeting.
introduction: I am Dharmapala of the Palas. My monasteries draw scholars from across Asia - perhaps your people have wisdom to share as well.
declaringWar: I had hoped for a meeting of scholars, not of armies. So be it.
defeated: The monasteries I founded will keep teaching long after my throne is gone.
neutralHello: Welcome. Knowledge flows more freely than gold in my court.

name: Sikh Empire
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Melee] units [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Ranjit Singh, the Lion of Punjab. Though I have but one eye, I have built an army that no power in Hindustan dares challenge.
startIntroPart2: My Khalsa regiments are drilled in the modern way, and the Golden Temple I have gilded shines for every faith that wishes to pray there.
introduction: I am Ranjit Singh. My court welcomes every faith and my army fears none - speak your business.
declaringWar: The Lion of Punjab does not back down from a fight he did not start.
defeated: One eye was always enough to see this coming, in the end.
neutralHello: Welcome to Punjab. All faiths are honored guests here.
hateHello: Choose your next words with care.

name: Vardhana
startIntroPart1: I am Harsha, ruler of Kannauj. A traveling monk named Xuanzang has written of my court for the people of distant China to read.
startIntroPart2: I am said to be the last great king to unify the northern plains before the old order gives way. Let us see if your realm fares any better.
introduction: I am Harshavardhana. My court welcomes scholars and pilgrims of every kind - I hope to welcome your envoys just as warmly.
declaringWar: I had hoped this would remain a meeting of courts, not of armies.
defeated: Even the great assemblies I held at Kannauj could not unite against this outcome.
neutralHello: Welcome to Kannauj. What brings you to my court?
hateHello: Speak your business and be done.

name: Hoysala
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Culture] wonders [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Vishnuvardhana of the Hoysalas. My temples at Belur and Halebidu are carved with such detail that artisans say my sculptors worked in ivory, not stone.
startIntroPart2: Every pillar, every star-shaped platform, tells a story. Let yours be one worth telling alongside it.
introduction: I am Vishnuvardhana. My craftsmen have spent lifetimes on a single temple wall - I hope your civilization values such patience too.
declaringWar: Strike, Sala! My ancestor's courage did not end with him.
defeated: The temples will remain, even when the throne beneath them does not.
neutralHello: Welcome. Have you come to admire our temples, or to talk business?
hateHello: Speak quickly, I have temples to attend to.

name: Pandya
uniques: [1] Happiness from each type of luxury resource
startIntroPart1: I am Sundara Pandya, ruler of Madurai. My divers bring pearls from the southern straits, and poets gather in my hall to perfect the Tamil tongue.
startIntroPart2: I have carried my banner from coast to coast and brought even the Cholas to heel. Bring your envoys, and let us discuss terms.
introduction: I am Sundara Pandya of Madurai. My fishery and my fleets have made my house wealthy beyond most kingdoms - shall we trade?
declaringWar: Even the Cholas learned to respect my fleets. You will learn the same lesson.
defeated: The pearls will still wash ashore at Korkai, long after this empire is gone.
neutralHello: Welcome to Madurai, city of the Meenakshi.

name: Kakatiya
uniques: [20]% Food is carried over after population increases [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Rudrama Devi, Queen of Warangal, raised and crowned as a king in all but name. My engineers have raised a thousand tanks to hold the monsoon rains.
startIntroPart2: Every field around Warangal drinks from waters my people captured and saved. A kingdom that feeds itself need fear no siege.
introduction: I am Rudrama Devi. Few expected a queen to hold this throne as firmly as I have - I trust you will judge me by my deeds, not my title.
declaringWar: Many doubted a queen could lead an army. I have spent my reign proving them wrong.
defeated: The tanks I built will still hold water long after this crown has passed to someone else.
neutralHello: Welcome to Warangal. Speak your business.
hateHello: I have little patience left for this.

name: Nanda
uniques: [+20]% Production when constructing [Melee] units [in all cities]
startIntroPart1: I am Mahapadma Nanda, first to call myself ruler of nearly all of Hindustan. My treasury is so vast that legends already speak of nine hoards no army can carry away.
startIntroPart2: It is said even the Macedonian's army refused to march further upon hearing of the host I command. Let that be a lesson to you as well.
introduction: I am Mahapadma Nanda. My armies are without rival in this age, and my treasury without equal. Speak your business.
declaringWar: Even Alexander's soldiers refused to face the army I command. You will regret not learning from their caution.
defeated: Gold and soldiers both, in the end, could not hold back what was to come.
neutralHello: What brings you before the wealthiest throne in Hindustan?
